blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how to find the smallest number that two or more numbers can divide without leaving a remainder? Or the largest number that can divide two or more numbers exactly? Let's explore LCM and HCF to find out!

blocks.markdown: In mathematics, the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) and the Highest Common Factor (HCF) are important concepts used to solve problems involving division and multiplication of numbers. Understanding these concepts helps in simplifying fractions, solving word problems, and more.

blocks.title: Definition of LCM
blocks.text: The Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of two or more numbers is the smallest number that is a multiple of each of the numbers.

blocks.markdown: To find the LCM, you can list the multiples of each number and identify the smallest multiple that appears in all lists. Alternatively, you can use the prime factorization method.

blocks.title: Definition of HCF
blocks.text: The Highest Common Factor (HCF), also known as the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD), of two or more numbers is the largest number that divides each of the numbers without a remainder.

blocks.title: Finding LCM and HCF
blocks.prompt: Find the LCM and HCF of 12 and 18.

steps.text: List the prime factors of each number: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3, 18 = 2 × 3 × 3.
For LCM, take the highest power of each prime: LCM = 2² × 3² = 36.
For HCF, take the lowest power of each common prime: HCF = 2¹ × 3¹ = 6.

blocks.answer: The LCM of 12 and 18 is 36, and the HCF is 6.

blocks.markdown: Understanding how to find the LCM and HCF can help solve word problems. For example, if you want to find out when two events will happen at the same time again, you can use the LCM.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember to check your prime factorization carefully. Mistakes in listing factors can lead to incorrect LCM or HCF calculations.

points: The LCM is the smallest common multiple of given numbers.
The HCF is the largest common factor of given numbers.
Use prime factorization to find LCM and HCF efficiently.
